title: Isomorphism descent for fixed finitely presented modules from an elementwise ring colimit
statement: Let J be a directed preorder and A_j commutative rings, with ring maps f_jl for j≤l satisfying f_jj=id and f_lm∘f_jl=f_jm. Let C be a commutative ring with compatible ring maps g_j:A_j→C. Assume every c∈C is g_j(a) for some j,a, and if g_j(a)=0 then f_jl(a)=0 at some l≥j. Fix i∈J and finitely presented A_i-modules P,N [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Give C and A_j (j≥i) their A_i-algebra structures using g_i and f_ij. If C⊗_{A_i}P≃_C C⊗_{A_i}N, there is a j≥i such that A_j⊗_{A_i}P≃_{A_j}A_j⊗_{A_i}N. The ring, index and two module universes are independent. This statement descends to one stage only; it assumes no tensor presentation of the ring diagram, no auxiliary coefficient rings and no flatness.

proof.text: The transition maps define a ring diagram with cocone (C,g). To verify its colimit property, define the map to any other compatible cocone on a representative g_j(a). Two representatives with the same image can be moved to a common stage; their difference vanishes in C, hence vanishes later by the zero assumption, so their images in the other cocone agree. Addition, multiplication, zero and one are preserved by choosing a common stage; uniqueness follows from the representative assumption. The same argument restricts to any upper tail. For a preorder use its poset reflection and choose one representative per class: mutually comparable transition maps are inverse by the system laws. Choose a common maximum universe and use ULift on the rings, indices and modules to fit the categorical interface; ULift equivalences transport the eventual conclusion back.

Apply the map-descent clause of finitePresentation_descent_directedColimit to the given equivalence and its inverse. Move both descended maps to a common stage. Their extensions agree with the original maps, because the canonical comparison isomorphisms satisfy the unit-tensor equations and these determine a scalar-extension map.

The stage modules remain finitely presented by base change. Each composite becomes the identity after scalar extension to C. Apply the equality clause of finitePresentation_descent_directedColimit to each composite and the appropriate identity. Take a common upper bound for these two eventual equalities. Base change preserves composition and identity, so the two maps there are inverse. Their linear equivalence is the required conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_stage_equiv_of_elementwise_colimit
    {J : Type v} [Preorder J] [IsDirectedOrder J]
    (A : J → Type u) [∀ j, CommRing (A j)]
    (f : ∀ (j l : J), j ≤ l → A j →+* A l)
    (hself : ∀ j, f j j le_rfl = RingHom.id (A j))
    (hcomp : ∀ j l m (hjl : j ≤ l) (hlm : l ≤ m),
      (f l m hlm).comp (f j l hjl) = f j m (hjl.trans hlm))
    (C : Type w) [CommRing C] (g : ∀ j, A j →+* C)
    (hg : ∀ j l (hjl : j ≤ l), (g l).comp (f j l hjl) = g j)
    (hsurj : ∀ c : C, ∃ j a, g j a = c)
    (hzero : ∀ j a, g j a = 0 → ∃ (l : J) (hjl : j ≤ l), f j l hjl a = 0)
    (i : J) (P : Type x) (N : Type y) [AddCommMonoid P] [AddCommMonoid N]
    [Module (A i) P] [Module (A i) N]
    [Module.FinitePresentation (A i) P] [Module.FinitePresentation (A i) N]
    (e : letI : Algebra (A i) C := (g i).toAlgebra
      Nonempty (C ⊗[A i] P ≃ₗ[C] C ⊗[A i] N)) :
    ∃ (j : J) (hij : i ≤ j),
      letI : Algebra (A i) (A j) := (f i j hij).toAlgebra
      Nonempty (A j ⊗[A i] P ≃ₗ[A j] A j ⊗[A i] N)
